policy: Use sibling digital variants, release timing, and explicit physical state labels to narrow unsuffixed identities without promoting exact artwork equivalence. A separate source key for an accessory state is positive evidence that the unsuffixed key should not be mapped to that accessory-state family. Post-launch or later-continuity physical releases remain separate even when they share the character name.

systemic_findings: Sibling digital variant keys can provide negative constraints: when a corpus explicitly has MaceWindu_Cape, the unsuffixed MaceWindu record should not automatically map to cape-only physical releases.
Release chronology is necessary but not sufficient: a physical figure can predate game launch yet represent a later narrative continuity state.
Helmet, hand-color, cape, and print-generation differences remain visual/component questions when the source key is unsuffixed.
